concepts.description: Competing objective families — short-term output (acute) versus emergent long-horizon system properties like safety and sustainability (chronic) — that cannot all be maximized together and default toward sacrificing the chronic set unless it is explicitly prioritized.
concepts.title: Acute vs. Chronic Objectives

concepts.description: A concrete litmus test for whether a support structure genuinely preserves a person's autonomy or has quietly slid into paternalism — ask whether they can do an ordinary, harmless, self-directed thing (heat up a burrito at midnight) without needing permission.
concepts.title: Autonomy-Preservation Heuristic (the "Burrito Test")

concepts.description: The target objective for a personal PRE system is sustainable daily-life quality — mornings without dread, relationships worth staying in, a life that does not need numbing — not external milestones like albums, titles, or revenue that can coexist with a miserable baseline.
concepts.title: Blooming as Life Outcome (Not Achievement Milestone)

concepts.description: Once societal default social obligations are stripped away, explicitly decide which human connections you actually want — a partner, one friend, solitude, family trust — instead of maintaining relationships because they look normal.
concepts.title: Chosen Relationship Objectives

concepts.description: Acute objectives broadcast strong, familiar metrics while chronic protection lacks leading indicators — making chronic goals easier to defer until crisis, and making "invest in safety when least affordable" the default trap under production pressure.
concepts.title: Chronic-Objective Measurement Asymmetry

concepts.description: Refusing to hand off work you could do — even from good motives — is a form of gluttony that erodes the time and reflective space needed to serve chronic objectives and the main thing.
concepts.title: Delegation as Capacity Protection

concepts.description: A pre-prepared three-tier (green/yellow/red) classification of which demands can be dropped without real consequence, which are droppable depending on circumstances, and which cannot be dropped — decided in advance so the choice doesn't have to be made under duress.
concepts.title: Demand Triage by Droppability

concepts.description: Macro-level explicit goal rules and communicated intent (downward) versus micro-level sacrifice judgements and professional buffering (upward) — both needed to balance conflicting objectives, with over-reliance on upward resilience when downward is weak as a structural vulnerability.
concepts.title: Downward vs. Upward Resilience

concepts.description: A decision-oriented conception of well-being that weights every lived moment by its duration (plus time spent dwelling on it or downstream misery it causes), rather than letting memorable peaks and endings dominate the score.
concepts.title: Duration-Weighted Well-Being

concepts.description: When choosing goals or interventions, attention to a salient change makes its future impact on well-being look larger than it will be — especially for one-time purchases or status shifts whose novelty fades — while ongoing attention-demanding activities are less overrated.
concepts.title: Focusing Illusion in Objective Choice

concepts.description: Life-evaluation satisfaction depends heavily on whether stated goals were attained — especially for goals the person marked as important — so choosing objectives that are difficult to reach is a structural recipe for chronic dissatisfaction even when circumstances are objectively good.
concepts.title: Goal Attainability as a Satisfaction Driver

concepts.description: Two distinct constructs for judging whether life is going well — global retrospective satisfaction versus moment-to-moment affect — that diverge enough that optimizing one can miss or distort the other.
concepts.title: Life Evaluation vs. Experienced Well-Being

concepts.description: Treating universal likability as a life objective trades away boundaries, authenticity, and sustainable relationships — accepting that some people will dislike your true self is often the prerequisite for protecting what actually matters.
concepts.title: Likability as a Wrong Objective

concepts.description: Without a named primary contribution or objective, every request looks equally deserving of yes — the discipline of no protects the vital few by anchoring trade-offs to what actually matters.
concepts.title: Main Thing as Priority Anchor

concepts.description: A prioritisation framework for social environments: identify the smallest masking set each context truly requires, meet only that minimum, and reclaim authenticity everywhere else — trading acute social-performance cost only where the environment demands it.
concepts.title: Minimum-Masking Trade-Off

concepts.description: Under reduced capacity, set the day's goal at what is realistically achievable — not the full aspirational list — so chronic protection does not collapse into dread, freeze, and deadline-only action.
concepts.title: Minimum Viable Day Objective

concepts.description: Named baseline needs or practices that stay protected regardless of other demands — explicit chronic objectives that prevent "temporary" sacrifice from becoming permanent erosion.
concepts.title: Non-Negotiable Protection Targets

concepts.description: Judging an intervention or a stretch of effort by visible activity (hours logged, busyness, being seen to work hard) rather than by the actual outcome delivered is a systematic way to reward the wrong thing and mistake motion for progress.
concepts.title: Outcomes vs. Activity as the Evaluation Signal

concepts.description: The remembering self scores episodes by peak intensity and ending quality while largely ignoring duration — a System 1 bias that conflicts with stated values and produces systematically bad choices when used to plan future well-being.
concepts.title: Peak-End Rule and Duration Neglect

concepts.description: "Struggling to prioritize" often means refusing society's default ranking of work, relationships, or hustle — valid PRE objective-setting starts from what genuinely matters to this person, not expected hierarchies.
concepts.title: Personal Priority Over Social Default

concepts.description: The same visible move — stepping back from demanding activity — can be a genuine investment in a protected objective or a fear-driven hiding from one, and the two are easy to mistake for each other from the outside and even from the inside.
concepts.title: Purposeful Withdrawal vs. Avoidant Withdrawal

concepts.description: A five-part checklist for noticing when chronic life objectives are actually being met — including unplanned small moments, quiet baselines, and slow seasonal payoffs — so evaluation does not chase milestones while missing bloom already present.
concepts.title: Recognizing Life Bloom (Evaluation Heuristics)

concepts.description: When acute production demands override the buffer that should protect chronic safety margins — through absent expertise, fear of delay, or culture that punishes sacrifice — the system drifts toward catastrophe while everyone acts riskier than they would consciously choose.
concepts.title: Resilience Erosion Under Production Pressure

concepts.description: Distinguishes recovery activities that genuinely rebuild capacity from low-effort activities that give fleeting relief but leave a person more depleted, as a way to judge whether a self-care intervention is a real investment in sustainability or a short-term patch.
concepts.title: Restorative Rest vs. Cheap Rest

concepts.description: A diagnostic for deciding whether to keep pouring capacity into a demanding commitment — ask whether staying is actually required, or whether it's the rewards (status, income, momentum) doing the holding, since the latter is a voluntary trade dressed up as an obligation.
concepts.title: Reward-Trap vs. Genuine Duty

concepts.description: Deliberately relaxing acute production pressure to stay clear of chronic safety margins — a trade-off decision that often looks wasteful in hindsight and only works if the culture still rewards it when "nothing happened."
concepts.title: Sacrifice Judgements

concepts.description: One way to decompose "what needs protecting" into concrete life domains — physical, emotional, mental, social, and professional — usable as a checklist for whether an intervention or life setup is covering every front rather than only the one currently making noise.
concepts.title: Self-Care Domains as a Protection-Target Taxonomy

concepts.description: Clarify why a project exists and what done looks like before scheduling work — then map backward from the end state so trade-offs serve stated objectives instead of drifting task-by-task.
concepts.title: Success Criteria Before Commitment

concepts.description: Deliberately operating below maximum perceived effort, treating slack as built-in recovery capacity rather than waste, produces better sustained output than running at 100% until burnout forces a collapse.
concepts.title: Sustainable Effort Ceiling (the ~85% Rule)

concepts.description: Ambition needs a named objective and a stopping rule — unchecked drive for more status, scale, or achievement consumes everything, including satisfaction, relationships, and the original cause.
concepts.title: Tempered Ambition

concepts.description: A five-step audit of whether your surrounding environment — especially work, where many adults spend half their waking hours — supplies enough support and return on energy to let chronic life objectives thrive, or is quietly burning you out.
concepts.title: Testing Life Soil (Environment Audit)

concepts.description: Frames "merely getting by" and "thriving" as different destinations entirely, not points on the same scale — a reminder that a PRE system optimizing only for avoiding collapse can succeed at that and still fail the actual goal.
concepts.title: Thriving vs. Surviving as the Target Objective

concepts.description: The percentage of waking time spent in unpleasant affect — a duration- grounded metric of the experiencing self's burden, distinct from global life-satisfaction scores.
concepts.title: U-Index for Experienced Suffering

concepts.description: A prioritization heuristic for competing demands under fixed capacity — identify the small subset of tasks/objectives that actually matter and give them the lion's share of time and energy, rather than spreading effort evenly across everything that shows up.
concepts.title: Vital Few vs. Trivial Many
